transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. Lee. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Lee. Well, I'm here because... there's an ongoing situation at my residence. For months now, the property manager and certain individuals in my building have been actively trying to pressure me out of my apartment. 

They're doing it through a series of specific actions—using intentionally misdelivered mail, timed noises in the walls, and little, pointed comments from the neighbors. The management keeps offering these standard explanations or showing me paperwork to try and brush it off, but... I analyze systems and data for a living. No amount of their excuses changes the clear pattern I can see happening around me.
How long exactly have you been noticing these events with the mail, noises, and comments—when did it all first start?
It's been going on for about 11 months now. I'd say it all started... well, very shortly after I moved into this new apartment.
Besides the noises you mentioned in the walls, have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people around you don't seem to hear?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I don't hear voices or... phantom sounds, if that's what you're asking. The noises I'm talking about in the walls are actual, physical sounds—like deliberate thumping or scraping. Anyone standing in my living room would hear them if they were there at the time they happen. But no, I don't hear voices.
Aside from this situation with your apartment, has your ability to function at work or in your relationships changed at all over these 11 months?

No, not at all. Aside from the time I have to spend dealing with this apartment situation, my day-to-day life is exactly the same. I still manage all my own finances, I cook for myself, I keep all my appointments... and I can still discuss my consulting work, or even my painting, in a completely organized way. My ability to function hasn't changed.

latest_inference.note: Preserved occupational/social functioning over 11 months, absence of hallucinations or disorganized thought, and a circumscribed, systematized persecutory belief argue against schizophrenia (F20.0) and support a diagnosis of delusional disorder.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a fixed, non-bizarre persecutory delusion (belief that the property manager and neighbors are orchestrating a coordinated campaign via mail, noises, and comments to force her out) lasting 11 months—well beyond the 1-month threshold for delusional disorder. There are no hallucinations, no disorganized speech or behavior, and no negative symptoms. Functioning is preserved outside the delusional theme (intact work, self-care, social interaction), which argues against schizophrenia (F20) where deterioration in functioning and typically broader psychotic symptoms (hallucinations, disorganization) are expected. The circumscribed, systematized nature of the belief, plausible/non-bizarre content (a common paranoid theme of persecution), and preserved general functioning fit the criteria for Delusional Disorder, persecutory type (F22).
